plot: On a windy autumn night something knocks on Pip's roof at nine every night and nobody is ever there, with a mess of shells by her door each morning (planted early); night-shift Grumpy suspects Turbo, who rolls past at nine doing slow-race practice, but the knock comes while Turbo stands in front of them, so Grumpy lifts Pip on his hook to see the gutter full of walnuts from the tree across the lane; in the dark they spot a squirrel storing food for winter, and Pip and Grumpy move all forty-two walnuts into his old toolbox by the tree; then before sunrise Bertha honks that someone moved her bus stop and the whole school.

script.title: Who Knocks on Pip's Roof Every Night?
script.description: Something knocks on Pip's roof every night, and nobody is there. Inspector Bolt #36

set.place: Bakery Lane outside Pip's little house, across from the big walnut tree behind Benny's bakery, a windy autumn night until just before sunrise

beats.say: Knock, knock, knock! Grumpy, it's happening again! Hurry!
I'm here. I see your roof. And I see... nobody.
Every night at nine. And nobody is ever there!
It was a windy autumn night on Bakery Lane.
Grumpy was on night shift, so Pip had asked him to stay close.
Night shift is usually quiet. I like quiet.
Well, my roof doesn't!
Good evening. Pip told me about the knocking. Fascinating.
Tell me everything, Pip. Even the tiny things.
First it knocks. Then it rolls. Then it stops.
And every morning, there's a mess of shells by my door!
Shells? Shells from what?
I don't know! I sweep them away before breakfast.
Knocks, rolling and shells. But nobody to be seen. Hmm.
I've towed lots of things. Never a mystery knock.
Then, from down the lane, came a very slow... rumble.
Slow... slow... night practice! Never stop, Turbo!
Aha. A car rolling past at nine o'clock.
Every night since Clementine came! Slow-race training!
Turbo! Is it YOU knocking on my roof?
Me? I can't even reach your roof! It's way up there!
Hmm. Suspicious. Stay right where you are, show-off.
And just then, with Turbo standing right in front of them...
See? Not me! I didn't move one single wheel!
Turbo is cleared. Our knocker is still out there.
If we don't find it, I'll never sleep again! Never ever!
What is all this noise? Some of us sleep at night!
Sorry, Bertha! My roof is knocking again!
Roofs don't knock, sweetie. Something knocks ON them.
Oh, good evening, Bolt. Wait. Sorry. That's a mailbox.
I'm over here, Bertha.
Enough talking. We need to see the top of that roof.
But I'm too small. And it's so high up!
You're small. I have a hook. Hop on, Pip.
Grumpy had lifted cars all his life. But never this gently.
Higher... higher... I can see the gutter!
Grumpy, it's full! Round, brown, bumpy things!
Bumpy balls on a roof? That is not normal.
Are they eggs? Are they giant dinosaur eggs?!
Not in Wheelburg, Turbo. Procedure: look closer.
They're walnuts! Dozens and dozens of walnuts!
Walnuts? But there's no walnut tree by your house, Pip.
Then who is putting walnuts on Pip's roof?
A bird? But birds sleep at night, don't they?
The only walnut tree is behind Benny's bakery. Across the lane.
Everyone looked at the dark tree. Then back at the roof.
Somebody carries walnuts all the way over here? Every night?
And drops them. Knock, knock, roll!
And the shells by your door each morning? That's breakfast.
Breakfast for WHO? Bolt, tell us before I zoom!
Shh. Lights off, everyone. If we scare it, it won't come back.
So the friends switched off their lights. And waited. Very quietly.
Waiting is so hard. Slow practice. Slow practice...
Then a tiny grey tail ran along the edge of the roof.
A squirrel! With a walnut in her mouth!
She is hiding food for winter. Your gutter is her pantry.
A nine o'clock delivery, every night. She works harder than me.
She wasn't trying to scare me. She was getting ready!
Just like me with my big winter blanket, sweetie.
But a gutter is a terrible pantry! Everything rolls!
And when it rains, her walnuts will wash away. All of them!
Then let's give her a better pantry.
I have my old toolbox. Dry. Strong. No knocking.
Grumpy put the box on the old stump, right by the walnut tree.
Up on his hook, Pip moved the walnuts. One by one.
Forty-two walnuts! Here's your new home, Mrs. Squirrel!
Do you think she'll find them?
The tiny tail ran down the tree. Sniffed the box. And hopped in.
She likes it! HOORAY! Oh. Too loud. Sorry.
Shh. Night shift voice, Bertha.
She's like Clementine! Slow, steady, and never stops working!
No more knocking. I can finally sleep!
And no more sweeping shells before breakfast, sweetie.
Remember: a strange noise isn't scary once you know who's there.
Goodnight, Pip. Goodnight, squirrel. Goodnight, toolbox.
And for the first time in a week, Bakery Lane was quiet.
But just before sunrise, Bertha came honking down the lane.
Bolt! Somebody moved my bus stop! And the whole school too!
The school? Bertha, a school can't move.
Then why did I drive right past it three times?!
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
